summary: The study investigates the effects of RF power on the interfacial properties between Al2O3 and Si3N4 and on the memory properties in a MANOS structure. The Al2O3 films were deposited using remote plasma atomic layer deposition (RPALD) at various RF powers, and the interfacial reaction was found to be dependent on the RF power. The results show that higher RF power improves the interface quality by reducing the migration of Si and N atoms from Si3N4 to Al2O3, leading to enhanced program/erase speed.
evidence: The Al2O3 films were deposited on Si3N4 using remote plasma ALD. The basic cycle of Al2O3 deposition consisted of four steps: (i) TMA exposure, (ii) purging of the residual precursors and by-products from the chamber using Ar gas, (iii) exposure of the oxygen plasma and (iv) purging of the reactants and by-products from the chamber using Ar gas. The RF power was varied from 50 to 300 W. The interfacial reaction between Al2O3 and Si3N4 is dependent on the RF power. After applying 18 V, the program speed of Al2O3 with 100 W, 200 W and 300 W were 10−2 s, 10−5 s and 10−6 s, respectively.
